  Wendell G. Hoback, P.E.   Field Engineer of Record / Construction Observation Lead    Sundial Engineering & Survey

  Reggie Marlon             Project Manager (Prime Subdivision Improvements Contract)   Mesquite Basin Constructors, LLC

  Dolan Yates               Site Superintendent                                         Mesquite Basin Constructors, LLC

  Terrence Kolb             Construction Inspector, Development Review                  Clark County Public Works

  Insp. Chad Voight         Fire Prevention Inspector                                   Clark County Fire Department
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Distribution of these notes: attendees above, plus CCFD Fire Plans Examiner (Capt. Emmett Roark) and Sundial project file 2201-03.

2. County Submittal and Inspection Sequence

The construction inspection sequence was walked through by Terrence Kolb (Clark County Public Works — Development Review). The following items were agreed and will govern Phase 2 inspection administration:

2.1 Inspection request procedure.

Mesquite Basin will submit inspection requests through the County Public Works construction inspection portal not less than 48 hours in advance of the requested inspection window. Requests will cite the improvement plan sheet, station range, and item to be inspected. Sundial's field engineer will be copied on each request; where the field engineer's presence is required (e.g., subgrade acceptance, storm drain pressure test, pavement structural section) Sundial will attend jointly with the County inspector.

2.2 Progressive inspections during construction.

Phase 2 will be inspected on a rolling basis by item: rough grading and moisture-density; storm drain trench, bedding and pressure tests prior to backfill; curb-and-gutter forming; subbase; base; and pavement placement. County inspector will sign each item on County inspection form; Sundial will maintain the running set of signed reports in the construction record for Phase 2.

2.3 Pre-final inspection.

When the improvements listed on the approved plans are complete in the field — including punch-list-condition landscape, signing and striping, and the temporary construction stub at the north boundary as shown on the improvement plans — Callaway will submit a written request for pre-final inspection. County will schedule the pre-final walk within ten (10) working days of the request. Sundial and Mesquite Basin will attend. Any punch items identified will be logged on the County form on-site and returned to Callaway the same week.

2.4 Final inspection and acceptance.

Following completion of pre-final punch, Callaway will submit a written request for final inspection with a signed contractor statement that punch items are complete. County will schedule final inspection within ten (10) working days. On satisfactory final inspection, County Public Works will issue a written improvement acceptance letter under separate cover. It was noted that Phase 2 offsite improvements (Rainbow Blvd. frontage, curb return at Windmill Ln., traffic control device) may be finalled and accepted on a schedule independent of the onsite balance; the two acceptances will be handled as separate letters. This is consistent with the release provisions in the Phase 2 improvement agreement and performance bond.

2.5 Record drawings.

Sundial will prepare Phase 2 record drawings (as-builts) from contractor red-lines, field survey, and County inspection reports, for submission with the improvement acceptance package. Sundial will maintain a working red-line set at the trailer for the duration of construction; the general contractor will keep a mirrored set. Record drawings will be sealed and dated after final inspection.

3. Traffic Control and Access

3.1 Construction access — primary.

Primary construction ingress and egress for Phase 2 will be from Rainbow Blvd. at the approved Phase 2 entry throat. All haul routes into and out of the site will use this entry. A traffic control plan conforming to the MUTCD and Clark County Public Works standards has been submitted by Mesquite Basin and approved for the Rainbow Blvd. work zone (curb return, taper, and flagger station).

3.2 Temporary construction stub across undeveloped Phase 3.

A temporary construction stub will be graded and paved across the northern boundary of the built Phase 2 area, extending into and across the presently undeveloped Phase 3 parcel to tie back to Windmill Ln. This stub is called out on the approved improvement plans and shown on the traffic control exhibit distributed at the meeting.

Two uses of the stub were confirmed and agreed:

-   Construction traffic. The stub will serve as a secondary construction access for material deliveries and heavy equipment during Phase 2 construction, relieving the Rainbow Blvd. entry.

-   Secondary emergency access for occupied Phase 2. Once dwelling units in Phase 2 are occupied and while Phase 3 remains undeveloped ground, the stub will serve as the secondary point of access required by CCFD for Phase 2 emergency response.

Both uses are expressly temporary. The stub crosses ground that is planned for Phase 3 subdivision development. It exists only because the Phase 3 remainder is presently ungraded and open. When Phase 3 is developed the stub will be removed and superseded by whatever access configuration is approved for Phase 3 on its own merits. This limitation was discussed in the meeting and was subsequently confirmed in writing by CCFD.

CCFD approval status.

At the time of the meeting, the CCFD access approval for Phase 2 was under review. Following the meeting, CCFD issued its formal approval by letter dated 06/12/2023 (Capt. Emmett Roark, Fire Plans Examiner). The letter approves the secondary access configuration for Phase 2 as a temporary condition pending development of Phase 3. That temporary designation is acknowledged on the record. Callaway and Sundial will maintain the CCFD letter in the project record and will treat the stub as a Phase 2 arrangement only; nothing in the CCFD Phase 2 correspondence is to be read as approval of an access configuration for Phase 3.

3.3 Stub construction and maintenance.

Mesquite Basin will construct the stub to the section and alignment shown on the approved Phase 2 improvement plans (compacted aggregate base with a bituminous surface course of the section noted on Sheet C-6). The stub will be barricaded at the Phase 3-side terminus with a Type III barricade and CCFD-compliant emergency-access knock-down gate. The stub will be maintained by Callaway for the duration of Phase 2 occupancy and until Phase 3 construction commences. Weekly inspection of the stub surface and barricade will be logged by Mesquite Basin during construction and by Callaway/HOA thereafter.

3.4 Signage.

"Emergency Access Only — No Public Through-Access" signage will be posted at the stub in both directions, per CCFD sign schedule. Contractor construction-access signage will be posted separately during the construction period only.

4. BMP Installation Sequence per SWPPP

The project Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP), as authored by Sundial and covered under the NDEP General Permit NVR100000 Notice of Intent for Desert Sage Ranch, governs installation and sequencing of construction stormwater BMPs. The following sequence was walked and agreed on-site:

4.1 Prior to any grading disturbance.

The following perimeter and inlet-protection BMPs will be installed and inspected before any Phase 2 earthwork begins:

-   Silt fence and reinforced silt fence along the downgradient (south and west) perimeter of the Phase 2 disturbance area, as shown on the SWPPP site map.

-   Stabilized construction entrance (rock pad with wheel-wash provision) at the Rainbow Blvd. primary construction entry.

-   Stabilized construction entrance (rock pad) at the temporary stub terminus at Windmill Ln.

-   Inlet protection (sandbag berm or filter insert) at all existing off-site catch basins within 100 ft of the disturbance boundary along Rainbow Blvd. and Windmill Ln.

-   Concrete washout containment at the location shown on the SWPPP site map, off the primary construction entry.

Sundial's field engineer will walk the perimeter BMPs with Mesquite Basin's superintendent and sign the SWPPP inspection log the day the perimeter is complete and before earthwork disturbance begins.

4.2 During mass grading.

Track-out control at both construction entries will be inspected daily by Mesquite Basin and after each significant rainfall event. Wind-erosion control (application of water and, where directed, tackifier) will follow the schedule in the SWPPP and the requirements of the Clark County Department of Environment and Sustainability dust control permit for the site.

4.3 As storm drain becomes operational.

As Phase 2 catch basins are installed, inlet protection (gravel bag or filter fabric type as noted in the SWPPP) will be placed at each basin the same day the frame and grate are set. Protection will remain in place until final stabilization or until paving is complete, whichever is later.

4.4 Stabilization.

Temporary stabilization of disturbed areas that will remain inactive for more than fourteen (14) days will be by application of tackifier or hydromulch, per the SWPPP. Final stabilization will be by landscape installation in improved areas and by soil binder / gravel treatment on Phase-2-facing slopes of the Phase 3 remainder that are disturbed by grading of the temporary stub.

4.5 Inspections and records.

Mesquite Basin will conduct SWPPP inspections weekly and within 24 hours after any rainfall of 0.25 inch or greater, log each inspection on the SWPPP inspection form, and correct deficiencies within the timeframes specified in the SWPPP. Sundial will spot-audit inspections at not less than a monthly interval. All SWPPP records will be kept at the site trailer and available for review by NDEP or Clark County inspectors.

4.6 Notice of Termination.

When Phase 2 improvements reach final stabilization and the improvements are accepted, Sundial will prepare and file a Notice of Termination with NDEP under NVR100000 to close construction stormwater coverage for the Phase 2 area of disturbance. The Notice of Termination will be limited to the Phase 2 area of disturbance and will be filed in the project record.

5. Utility Coordination

5.1 Wet utilities.

-   Water. Water main installation is by Mesquite Basin under LVVWD standard specifications, on the alignments and to the sizes shown on the approved plans. Pressure test and disinfection to LVVWD standards; LVVWD field acceptance required prior to service connection. LVVWD inspector to be scheduled by Mesquite Basin through the LVVWD construction desk with 48-hour notice.

-   Sewer. Sewer main installation is by Mesquite Basin under CCWRD standard specifications. Mandrel test and low-pressure air test on completed reaches; CCWRD field acceptance required prior to backfill approval. Manhole vacuum test on all manholes. CCWRD inspection scheduled through CCWRD Plan Review Engineer's office (Vince Alarid, CCWRD).

5.2 Dry utilities (joint trench).

Composite dry utility plan (electric — NV Energy; gas — Southwest Gas; telecom — CenturyLink and Cox) is on file. Joint trench and conduit installation to be sequenced by Mesquite Basin after storm drain and sewer are backfilled and prior to base course. Each dry utility purveyor will inspect its own facilities prior to trench closure. The dry utility coordinator will attend a joint trench pre-installation meeting on-site before joint trench work begins; date to be set by Mesquite Basin.

5.3 Locating existing.

Blue-stake / USA North 811 will be called by Mesquite Basin for each work area 48 hours in advance of digging. Sundial will provide the contractor with the survey-verified locations of the offsite tie-ins at Rainbow Blvd.

5.4 Utility crossing conflicts.

Any utility crossing conflict identified in the field will be reported by Mesquite Basin to Sundial the same day. Sundial will provide a resolution or field revision within 24 hours where possible; where a field revision affects an approved plan sheet, Sundial will issue a numbered field revision memo and copy the County construction inspector.

5.5 Fire protection features.

Hydrant locations and fire department connections were walked by CCFD (Insp. Voight). Hydrant spacing on the plans meets CCFD standard. Hydrants are to be operational (flushed, tested, and flowed) prior to combustible construction commencing above the foundation on any dwelling unit. Hydrant flow test to be witnessed by CCFD and coordinated by Callaway's builder.

 The Enterprise Town Advisory Board (TAB) is an appointed body that advises the Clark County Board of County
 Commissioners and the Planning Commission on land use, zoning, and community matters affecting the
 unincorporated Enterprise township. Meetings are open to the public and conducted in accordance with Nevada
 Open Meeting Law.

 Section 1 — 2026 Regular Meeting Calendar
 Regular meetings are held on the third Wednesday of each month at 6:00 PM at the Enterprise Library unless
 otherwise noticed. Notice of any change in date, time, or location shall be posted in accordance with NRS Chapter

 Calendar Notes
 1. Agenda posting. The agenda for each regular meeting shall be posted no later than 5:00 PM on the tenth (10th)
     calendar day preceding the meeting, at the Enterprise Library, at the Clark County Government Center, and to
     the State of Nevada public notice website, together with any accompanying meeting materials.
 2. Public comment sign-up. Individuals wishing to be recognized under the public comment periods must submit a
     speaker card to the Clerk no later than 5:30 PM on the day of the meeting. Cards received after that time will be
     accepted at the discretion of the Chair as time permits.
 3. Holidays and cancellations. Should a regular meeting date fall on a recognized County holiday, or should the
     venue be unavailable, the Clerk will reschedule and re-notice the meeting in accordance with Nevada Open
     Meeting Law. Any special or workshop meetings will be noticed separately.

  4. Accommodation requests. Requests for reasonable accommodation, interpretation, or auxiliary aids must be
     received by the Clerk at (702) 555-4620 at least seventy-two (72) hours prior to the meeting.


 Section 2 — Standard Agenda Template
 The following order of business applies to each regular meeting. The Chair may reorder items for the convenience of
 the public or applicants, subject to a proper motion of the Board.


                   ENTERPRISE TOWN ADVISORY BOARD — REGULAR MEETING

      Date:          [ ______________________________ ]
      Time:          6:00 PM
      Location:      Enterprise Library, 25 E. Shelbourne Ave., Las Vegas, NV 89123
      Chair:         Lorna Pike

 (a) Call to Order and Roll Call
 The Chair calls the meeting to order and the Clerk records attendance of Board members. A quorum consists of a
 majority of appointed members.
 (b) Pledge of Allegiance
 (c) Approval of Minutes
 Consideration and approval of the minutes of the preceding regular meeting.
 (d) Public Comment (Agenda Items)
 Any member of the public may address the Board on matters appearing on the current agenda. Speakers are limited
 to two (2) minutes per speaker and shall state name and area of residence for the record. Comment shall be directed
 to the Chair, not to individual Board members, staff, or applicants.
 (e) Old Business
 Items continued or held over from prior meetings, including any application returned to the Board for further
 consideration.
 (f) New Business — Planning Items
 Presentation of, and Board recommendation on, land use applications forwarded by Clark County Comprehensive
 Planning. Typical items include:
     • Variance applications
     • Use permit and conditional use applications
     • Waiver requests (including waivers of development standards)
     • Design review items requiring TAB recommendation
     • Zone change and text amendment applications
     • Tentative and final map items referred for community input
     • Extension of time requests
 For each item the Board will hear a staff summary, an applicant presentation, public testimony (two minutes per
 speaker), Board questions and deliberation, and a motion. The Board's action on each planning item is a
 recommendation and is forwarded, together with the record of testimony, to the Clark County Planning
 Commission and/or the Board of County Commissioners for final action.
 (g) Public Comment on Non-Agenda Items
 Any member of the public may address the Board on any matter within the jurisdiction of the Board that does not
 appear on the current agenda. Speakers are limited to two (2) minutes per speaker. No action may be taken by the

Enterprise Town Advisory Board | 2026 Calendar & Standard Agenda                                               Page 2
  Board on matters raised under this item; however, the Chair may direct that a matter be placed on a future agenda for
 consideration.
 (h) TAB Member Reports and Announcements
 Reports by individual Board members on community meetings attended, correspondence received, and matters for
 possible future agendas. Announcements by the Clerk regarding upcoming meetings, deadlines, and County notices.
 (i) Adjournment


 Section 3 — Process Notes for Applicants, Agencies, and the Public
 Submitting an Application for TAB Recommendation
 Any application requiring a recommendation of the Enterprise Town Advisory Board — including variance
 applications, use permits, waivers, design review items, and zone changes — must be filed with Clark County
 Comprehensive Planning and referred to the TAB by staff. To appear on a given meeting agenda, the complete
 application package (including all exhibits and any required neighborhood meeting summary) must be received by
 Comprehensive Planning no later than 21 days prior to the meeting date. This period is necessary to permit staff
 review, agenda preparation, and the ten-day posting required by Nevada Open Meeting Law. Applications received
 after the 21-day cutoff will be scheduled for the next available meeting.
 Design review items — including but not limited to architectural design review, landscape design review, and site
 plan review items referred to the Board — follow the same 21-day submittal window. Applicants are strongly
 encouraged to coordinate with the assigned planner prior to the deadline to confirm that the record is complete.
 Effect of TAB Action
 TAB recommendations are advisory to the Clark County Board of County Commissioners and to the Clark County
 Planning Commission. The Board of County Commissioners and the Planning Commission retain final authority
 over all land use applications within their respective jurisdictions. The record of the TAB meeting — including any
 recommendation, the vote, and the public testimony — is transmitted with the staff report to the final
 decision-making body.
 Continuances
 An applicant may request a continuance to a later meeting. Continuance requests should be submitted in writing to
 Comprehensive Planning at the earliest practicable date and, absent good cause shown, no later than seven (7) days
 before the scheduled meeting. The Board may also continue an item on its own motion.
 Public Testimony
 The Board welcomes public testimony on all matters within its jurisdiction. To ensure that all persons wishing to
 speak have an opportunity to do so, the Chair enforces the two-minute per speaker limit under items (d) and (g).
 Written comment may be submitted to the Clerk at any time prior to the meeting at (702) 555-4620 and will be
 entered into the record. Group presentations may be arranged in advance with the Chair through the Clerk.
 Neighborhood Meetings
 For applications for which County policy requires or recommends a pre-application neighborhood meeting, the
 applicant is encouraged to hold that meeting no fewer than fourteen (14) days before the TAB meeting and to include
 a summary of the meeting, attendance, and issues raised in the submittal package.
 Recording
 Meetings are audio-recorded and, where equipment permits, video-recorded. Recordings and approved minutes are
 retained by the Clerk and made available upon request in accordance with Nevada public records law.

The Las Vegas Valley Water District (the “District”) has completed its review of the request submitted on behalf of
Callaway Land Partners for water service to Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3, a proposed 60-lot single-family residential
subdivision on the 40.0-acre remainder parcel identified above, located within the unincorporated community of
Enterprise, Clark County, Nevada. The parcel lies wholly within the District’s certificated service area.

Capacity and Commitment
Based upon the District’s most recent modeling of the transmission and distribution system serving the Rainbow
Boulevard corridor, and upon anticipated demand computed at the District’s per-lot design factors for detached
single-family residential use, the District confirms that sufficient supply, storage, and delivery capacity exists to serve the
60 lots proposed for Desert Sage Ranch Phase 3.
Accordingly, the District hereby issues this will-serve letter as a commitment of water service to the parcel identified
above, for the 60 residential lots and associated common-area irrigation demand indicated in the developer’s submittal,
subject to the standard conditions set forth below.

Standard Conditions of Service
This will-serve commitment is issued subject to, and conditioned upon, the following:

1. Connection and capital fees. Payment in full of all connection charges, capital contribution fees, meter installation
    fees, and any applicable regional infrastructure charges in effect at the time each service connection is made, in
    accordance with the District’s Service Rules then in force.
2. Service agreement. Execution by the developer of the District’s standard Developer Service Agreement, including
     all customary indemnities, easement dedications within the plat, and provisions for testing, disinfection, and
     conveyance of onsite mains to the District upon acceptance.
3. Onsite mains and appurtenances. Design, construction, testing, and disinfection of all onsite water mains, valves,
    hydrants, service laterals, and appurtenances in strict conformance with the District’s current Design and
    Construction Standards. Improvement plans must be submitted to the District’s Engineering Services group for
    review and approval prior to construction; District field inspection is required through acceptance.
4. Backflow protection. Provision of backflow prevention assemblies at all locations required by the Uniform
    Plumbing Code, the Nevada Administrative Code, and the District’s Cross-Connection Control Program, including
    — without limitation — service to the HOA common-area irrigation system. Assemblies shall be of a type
    approved by the University of Southern California Foundation for Cross-Connection Control and Hydraulic
    Research and shall be tested by a certified tester on the schedule required by the District.
5. Fire flow. Fire flow demands shall be established in coordination with the Clark County Fire Department; hydrant
     spacing, size, and residual pressure requirements shall be as approved by the fire authority having jurisdiction and
     shall be consistent with the District’s Design and Construction Standards.

Comprehensive Planning is in receipt of the written application submitted by Callaway Land Partners on
October 28, 2024, requesting an Extension of Time in which to present the first final map in the series under
TM-22-500041. This letter is the Department's response and, together with your application, constitutes the
official record for the tentative map file with respect to the extension question and the subsequent map clock.
                                   1. Governing statute — NRS 278.360

The extension mechanism available under Nevada law is set forth in NRS 278.360. In pertinent part, the statute
provides:

       "The governing body may, upon written application filed after the applicable period has expired,
       grant an extension of not more than two (2) years. An extension shall not be granted before the
       applicable presentation period has expired."

The statute is written in mandatory terms and its two operative preconditions — a written application, and a filing
date after the applicable period has expired — are jurisdictional. The County has no discretion to relax them.


                              2. Disposition of the 10/28/2024 application

Because the Callaway Land Partners application of 10/28/2024 was filed before the applicable presentation
period had expired, the County is without authority to act on it on the merits. The application is not properly
before the County until the applicable period has expired, and the County therefore declines to act on the
request in advance of the presentation period. This is a jurisdictional disposition, not a rejection on the merits.

Nothing in this letter forecloses any future written application filed by Callaway Land Partners in compliance with
the statutory precondition, if and when the applicable period has expired and Callaway has cause to seek relief.
Any such future application would be evaluated on its own record and on the standards then applicable.


                          3. Presentation of the first final map in the series

The Department has been advised, and the Clark County Recorder's index confirms, that the first final map in
the series under TM-22-500041 — Desert Sage Ranch Phases 1 & 2 (100 residential lots on approximately 100
acres, together with a remainder parcel for future Phase 3) — has been presented and recorded of record. The
applicant may consult the Recorder's public index for the recording particulars.

The four-year first-map presentation clock that runs from the date of tentative map approval has accordingly
been satisfied and is no longer at issue with respect to Desert Sage Ranch.


                           4. Presentation clock for successive final maps

The applicable statutory framework under NRS 278.360 continues to govern the tentative map. The applicant
and its design consultants are directed to confirm the operative presentation deadline for any successive map
with Comprehensive Planning. Failure to timely present a successive map within the applicable statutory period
would terminate all further proceedings under TM-22-500041.

    All work shall conform to Clark County Code Title 30, Chapter 30.64 (Landscaping, Walls and Buffers), the
    Southern Nevada Regional Plant List, and the Clark County Standard Drawings current at the date of
    approval.
    Turf placement complies with Clark County Code sec. 30.64.030(j), which permits turf in conjunction with
    cemeteries, parks and schools and prohibits turf within ten feet of a street or curb. Restrictions of sec.

    spray-irrigated on a dedicated station; all other planted areas shall be drip-irrigated on separate stations.

    frontage, measured continuously along each dedicated right-of-way.

8880 W. Sunset Road, Suite 400

cc: Mr. Max Braddock, PM — Sundial Engineering & Survey

Re: Desert Sage Ranch HOA — Phase 3 Park Landscape and Nonfunctional Turf Conversion
Cost

Dear Garrett,

Thank you for the update at last week’s coordination call and for keeping our office in the loop as the Phase
3 improvement plans and final map move through their current review cycle. The Phase 1/2 Board and the
homeowners we work with share Callaway’s interest in a smooth recordation, and this letter is offered in
that spirit — as an early flag on a couple of items the Board would like to have addressed before Phase 3
crosses the counter, so that questions from the community do not surface at a less convenient moment.

Nonfunctional turf conversion — Phase 1/2 common areas. The Board reviewed the Southern Nevada
Water Authority nonfunctional turf compliance materials at its October regular meeting and has taken
counsel from our office and from a landscape contractor on what the 12/31/2026 deadline means for the
association. Our understanding, and the advice we have been given, is that any turf conversion required in
the existing Phase 1/2 common areas — parcels the association owns and maintains — is a cost that falls to
the association rather than to the developer, and the Board has begun budgeting on that basis. Current
pricing we have collected from two local contractors for turf-to-desert conversion in park settings runs on
the order of $2.85 per square foot, inclusive of removal, soil prep, drip retrofit, decomposed granite, and a
modest planting palette. Even the areas the Board expects to keep as functional playground turf still leave a
scope that, when combined with adjacent landscape refresh the community has been discussing, is projected
to reach into the tens of thousands of dollars for the association in the next reserve cycle. The Board is
prepared to absorb its share of that obligation. It has, however, asked me to make sure the developer’s team
is aware that the community is watching how the Phase 3 landscape reads against the same standard.

Phase 3 park — playground amenities. The Board’s second and more forward-looking question concerns
the Phase 3 park. On the current landscape sheets circulated at the September coordination meeting, the
Phase 3 park parcel reads to us as a turfed lawn without the play equipment the Phase 1/2 park carries. The
Phase 1/2 park was built with slides, swings, and climbing structures inside a bordered play area, and in
every homeowner survey we have run since 2024 that playground has come up as one of the two or three
most-used common-area amenities in the community — ahead of the trail loop and the ramada, and
comparable to the pool. Families with children moved to Desert Sage Ranch in part because of it.

We are asking, plainly, whether the Phase 3 park will include the same playground amenities — slides,
swings, and climbing structures within a designated play area — as the Phase 1/2 park. The Board would
like to be able to tell homeowners that the answer is yes. If the current design does not carry those amenities
 forward, the Board would appreciate the opportunity to sit down with your landscape architect and Mr.
Braddock’s team before the resubmittal is finalized, to understand the reasoning and to discuss whether there
is room to reintroduce them. We recognize that the two questions above are related in ways that the Board
does not need to spell out here; the design team will see them, and we trust the design team to weigh them.

Enterprise Town Advisory Board — 11/18/2026. In the interest of transparency, and so this does not come
as a surprise: a group of Phase 1/2 homeowners has organized to attend the Enterprise Town Advisory Board
meeting on 11/18/2026 and to address the Phase 3 park treatment during public comment. They intend to
speak respectfully and to focus on the amenity question rather than on personalities or on Callaway’s
broader entitlement, but they will speak, and the local paper occasionally covers TAB comment. The Board
has not endorsed any particular position for the homeowners to take; it has, however, declined to discourage
them from attending. I mention it now, rather than the week before, so that the Callaway team and Sundial
have time to consider whether an outreach conversation ahead of that meeting would be useful.

Offer to coordinate. Our office is available to host a joint working session at the Sagebrook offices in the
next two to three weeks, at whatever time suits Callaway and Sundial, with the Phase 1/2 Board president
and our landscape committee chair present. If it would help, I can also circulate the homeowner survey
results and the two contractor quotes referenced above in advance of any such meeting, so that the numbers

 DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS, AND RESTRICTIONS
                                 FOR DESERT SAGE RANCH

                          WITH COMMON AREA MAINTENANCE EXHIBIT

THIS DECLARATION OF COVENANTS, CONDITIONS, AND RESTRICTIONS FOR DESERT SAGE RANCH
(this "Declaration") is made and executed this 23rd day of December, 2024, by CALLAWAY LAND PARTNERS,
a Nevada limited liability company, having a principal place of business at 8880 W. Sunset Road, Suite 400, Las
Vegas, NV 89148 (the "Declarant"), with reference to the facts recited below.



                                          ARTICLE I. RECITALS

A. Declarant is the owner in fee simple of certain real property situated in the unincorporated area of Clark
County, Nevada, being a portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., Clark County,
Nevada, consisting of approximately 140.0 acres and commonly known and identified as the Desert Sage
Ranch subdivision (the "Property").

B. Declarant has caused the Property to be subdivided into three (3) sequential phases, being Phase 1, Phase
2, and Phase 3, together comprising residential lots, common-area parcels, streetscape parcels, and dedicated
public rights-of-way, all as more particularly depicted on the recorded final map(s) of the Property.

C. Concurrently with the execution and recordation of this Declaration, the First Final Map for Desert Sage
Ranch, Phases 1 and 2, being Map No. NFM-24-0118, is being recorded in the Office of the Clark County
Recorder at Book 175, Page 60 of Official Records ("First Final Map"). This Declaration is intended to be
recorded contemporaneously with, and to encumber the property depicted upon, the First Final Map, and to run
with and encumber the entire Property, including the Phase 3 remainder to be depicted on a successive final
map, upon its recordation.

D. It is the intention of Declarant to establish and impose upon the Property a general plan for the improvement,
protection, maintenance, and administration of Desert Sage Ranch as a planned residential community,
including without limitation the ownership and maintenance of certain common areas by a community
association formed for that purpose.
 E. Declarant intends that the covenants, conditions, restrictions, easements, assessments, charges, and liens
set forth below shall run with the land and be binding upon all persons or entities having or acquiring any right,
title, or interest in the Property or any portion thereof, and shall inure to the benefit of each Owner thereof.

F. Declarant has caused this Declaration to be prepared by Adrienne Vogel, Esq., of Vogel & Marsh LLP,
outside counsel to Declarant, in the manner set forth herein.

NOW, THEREFORE, Declarant hereby declares that the Property shall be held, sold, conveyed, encumbered,
hypothecated, leased, used, occupied, and improved subject to the following covenants, conditions, restrictions,
easements, assessments, charges, and liens, all of which are declared to be in furtherance of a general plan
and scheme for the subdivision, improvement, and sale of the Property.



                                          ARTICLE II. DEFINITIONS

The following capitalized terms, when used in this Declaration, shall have the meanings set forth in this Article II.
Terms not otherwise defined herein shall have the meanings customarily ascribed to them under Chapter 116 of
the Nevada Revised Statutes.

Section 2.1. "Articles." The Articles of Incorporation of the Association, as the same may be amended from
time to time.

Section 2.2. "Association." Desert Sage Ranch Community Association, a Nevada nonprofit corporation,
being the community association formed by Declarant to administer, own, and maintain the Common Area and
to enforce the terms of this Declaration. The Association is the community association contemplated by NRS
Chapter 116. All references herein to "HOA" mean the Association.

Section 2.3. "Board." The Board of Directors of the Association.

Section 2.4. "Bylaws." The Bylaws of the Association, as the same may be amended from time to time.

Section 2.5. "Common Area." All real property (including any Improvements thereon) that is (i) owned by the
Association in fee simple, or (ii) held by the Association under an easement, license, or maintenance obligation
for the common use and enjoyment of the Owners. Common Area expressly includes, without limitation, the
Common-Area Park, the Streetscape Common Area, the Entry Feature, and all landscaping, irrigation
infrastructure, hardscape, walls, monumentation, signage, and amenities located therein as installed by
Declarant or its successors. Common Area does not include any Lot or any portion of a public right-of-way
conveyed by dedication to Clark County or another public body.

Section 2.6. "Common-Area Park." The parcel of Common Area designated on the recorded final map as
Parcel A, being an active-use park parcel improved with landscaping, irrigation, and, as installed by Declarant,
any turf area and any playground amenities (which, where installed, may consist of slides, swings, and climbing
structures). Parcel A is owned by the Association and is not part of any Lot.

Section 2.7. "Declarant." Callaway Land Partners, a Nevada limited liability company, and its successors and
assigns to whom the rights of Declarant hereunder are expressly assigned in a recorded instrument.

Section 2.8. "Declaration." This Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Desert Sage
Ranch, together with all exhibits and attachments hereto and all amendments and supplements duly recorded.
 Section 2.9. "Entry Feature." The parcel of Common Area designated on the recorded final map as Parcel C,
being the community entry treatment situated at the intersection of Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, and
improved with entry monumentation, signage, walls, planting, irrigation, and accent lighting. Parcel C is owned
by the Association and is not part of any Lot.

Section 2.10. "Governing Documents." This Declaration, the Articles, the Bylaws, and the rules and
regulations of the Association, each as the same may be amended from time to time, together with all recorded
exhibits, plats, and supplemental declarations.

Section 2.11. "Improvement." Any structure, wall, fence, monument, sign, tree, shrub, turf, planting, irrigation
line, playground amenity, path, hardscape, or other tangible thing installed upon or affixed to the land.

Section 2.12. "Lot." Each numbered residential lot depicted upon a recorded final map of the Property and
intended for the construction and occupancy of a single detached residential dwelling. Each Lot is a separately
conveyable parcel; no Lot includes any portion of any Common Area, and no Common Area is any part of any
Lot.

Section 2.13. "Managing Agent." The community management firm engaged by the Association pursuant to a
written management agreement to perform the day-to-day administration of the Association's affairs, including
the maintenance and replacement obligations set forth in Article V. As of the date of this Declaration, the
Managing Agent is Sagebrook Community Management LLC, a Nevada limited-liability company, having offices
at 6280 S. Pecos Road, Suite 300, Las Vegas, NV 89120.

Section 2.14. "Map" or "Final Map." Any final subdivision map of any portion of the Property recorded in the
Office of the Clark County Recorder, including the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, recorded at Book
175, Page 60) and any successive final map for Phase 3.

Section 2.15. "Owner." The record holder of fee simple title to a Lot, excluding any person or entity holding title
solely as security for the performance of an obligation.

Section 2.16. "Property." All of the real property described in Article III below and shown upon the Map(s),
together with all Improvements thereon, and any additional property annexed hereto in accordance with this
Declaration.

Section 2.17. "Streetscape Common Area." Those parcels or strips of Common Area situated between the
back-of-curb of a public street and the front or side lot lines of the adjoining Lots (or, where applicable, between
the back-of-curb and a perimeter community wall), extending along all frontage of the Property, and improved
with sidewalks (where the sidewalk is not within the dedicated public right-of-way), desert planting, street trees,
and drip irrigation. Each Streetscape Common Area parcel is owned by the Association and is not part of any
Lot.



                                ARTICLE III. PROPERTY DESCRIPTION

Section 3.1. Legal Description of the Property. The Property subject to this Declaration is that certain real
property situated in the unincorporated area of Clark County, State of Nevada, more particularly described as
follows:

       A portion of Section 27, Township 22 South, Range 60 East, M.D.M., Clark County, Nevada,
       containing approximately 140.0 acres, together with all easements, tenements, hereditaments, and
       appurtenances thereunto belonging, commonly known as Desert Sage Ranch, situated at the
       intersection of Rainbow Boulevard and Windmill Lane, Las Vegas, Nevada 89178.
 Section 3.2. Phasing. The Property is subject to development in three sequential phases:

(a) Phase 1 — as more particularly depicted upon the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, Book 175, Page
60), consisting of residential Lots, streetscape and open-space Common Area, and dedicated street
rights-of-way, all as shown upon Sheets 2 through 4 of the First Final Map.

(b) Phase 2 — as more particularly depicted upon the First Final Map (Map No. NFM-24-0118, Book 175, Page
60), consisting of residential Lots, streetscape and open-space Common Area (including the Common-Area
Park designated Parcel A, the shared Detention Facility designated Parcel B, and the Entry Feature designated
Parcel C), and dedicated street rights-of-way, all as shown upon Sheets 2 through 4 of the First Final Map.

(c) Phase 3 — that portion of the Property consisting of approximately 40.0 acres, presently identified by Clark
County Assessor's Parcel Number 177-27-201-001, to be subdivided into approximately sixty (60) half-acre
residential Lots, together with associated streetscape Common Area and dedicated street rights-of-way, all to be
depicted upon a successive final map to be recorded by Declarant. Upon recordation of the Phase 3 final map,
the Lots and Common Area created thereby shall automatically be and become subject to this Declaration
without the necessity of any further instrument.

Section 3.3. Annexation of Successive Phases. Declarant reserves the right, exercisable in its sole discretion
and without the consent of any Owner, Mortgagee, or the Association, to annex Phase 3 (and any lawful
reconfiguration thereof) to the regime of this Declaration by recordation of a Supplemental Declaration in the
Office of the Clark County Recorder that (i) identifies the annexed property by reference to the recorded final
map, and (ii) states that the annexed property is thereby made subject to this Declaration.

Section 3.4. Public Rights-of-Way. All streets, alleys, and other public rights-of-way depicted upon any Map
are conveyed by dedication to Clark County or the applicable public body. No such dedicated area is Common
Area, and the Association bears no maintenance obligation for improvements accepted for public maintenance
within any such dedicated area, except as provided by written agreement with the applicable public body.



                                     ARTICLE IV. COMMON AREAS

Section 4.1. Establishment of Common Area. Declarant hereby establishes and dedicates for the common
use and enjoyment of the Owners, and conveys to the Association concurrently herewith and by the recordation
of each applicable Map, all Common Area, in fee simple, free and clear of all monetary encumbrances other
than the lien of current taxes and assessments not yet delinquent and matters of record specifically noted upon
the Map.

Section 4.2. Parcel A — Common-Area Park. The parcel designated Parcel A on the First Final Map (and as
reflected in Exhibit B hereto) is hereby established as the Common-Area Park. Parcel A is owned in fee simple
by the Association and is not part of any Lot. Parcel A is improved by Declarant with landscaping, irrigation, and,
as installed by Declarant, any turf area and any playground amenities (which, where installed by Declarant, may
consist of slides, swings, and climbing structures). All landscaping, irrigation infrastructure, turf, planting,
hardscape, and playground amenities installed upon Parcel A, as and where installed, constitute Common Area
Improvements owned by the Association.

Section 4.3. Parcel C — Entry Feature. The parcel designated Parcel C on the First Final Map (and as
reflected in Exhibit B hereto) is hereby established as the Entry Feature. Parcel C is owned in fee simple by the
Association and is not part of any Lot. Parcel C is improved by Declarant with community entry monumentation,
community identification signage, decorative perimeter walls, drip-irrigated desert planting, and accent lighting.
All Improvements installed upon Parcel C constitute Common Area Improvements owned by the Association.
 Section 4.4. Streetscape Common Area. The streetscape strips depicted on each recorded Map along all
frontage of the Property, being situated between the back-of-curb of the adjoining public street and the front or
side lot lines of the abutting Lots (or the adjoining perimeter wall, where applicable), are hereby established as
Streetscape Common Area. Each such strip is owned in fee simple by the Association, is not part of any Lot,
and is improved by Declarant with street trees, drip-irrigated desert planting, decorative rock cover, and, where
applicable, community perimeter wall and sidewalk. The Streetscape Common Area extends continuously along
the entire street frontage of the Property, in the extent depicted upon the First Final Map and upon any
successive final map recorded for Phase 3.

Section 4.5. Distinct from Lots. The Common-Area Park (Parcel A), the shared Detention Facility (Parcel B),
the Entry Feature (Parcel C), and each Streetscape Common Area parcel are each Common Area owned and
maintained by the Association, and no such parcel is a Lot or any part of a Lot. No Owner has any right, by
virtue of ownership of a Lot, to construct, remove, alter, replace, or reconfigure any Improvement located within
any Common Area.

Section 4.6. Easements Appurtenant. Every Owner shall have a nonexclusive easement of use and
enjoyment in and to the Common Area, appurtenant to and passing with title to such Owner's Lot, subject to the
terms of this Declaration and the rules and regulations of the Association.

Section 4.7. Reserved Easements. Declarant reserves to itself, the Association, the Managing Agent, and their
respective employees, agents, and contractors, a perpetual easement over, upon, across, and through each
Common Area parcel for the purposes of installing, inspecting, maintaining, repairing, and replacing Common
Area Improvements, including without limitation landscaping, irrigation infrastructure, turf, planting, and
playground amenities, as installed.

Section 4.8. No Partition. The Common Area shall remain undivided. No Owner or other person shall bring any
action for the partition or division of the Common Area, and each Owner waives any right of partition such
Owner may hold at law or in equity.



                         ARTICLE V. MAINTENANCE AND REPLACEMENT

Section 5.1. Association Responsibility. The Association shall be responsible for the continuous and ongoing
maintenance, repair, and replacement of the Common Area and all Improvements located thereon, including
without limitation:

(a) all landscaping within the Common Area, including all turf, planting, groundcover, shrubs, and trees, as and
where installed;

(b) all irrigation infrastructure within the Common Area, including without limitation mainline, laterals, valves,
valve boxes, backflow prevention assemblies, controllers, wiring, and emitters;

(c) all playground amenities located within the Common Area, as installed, including without limitation slides,
swings, climbing structures, and any associated resilient surfacing, safety zone materials, and containment
curbing;

(d) all hardscape within the Common Area, including sidewalks (where not within a dedicated public right-of-way
accepted for public maintenance), walls, monumentation, signage, benches, and accent lighting; and

(e) all other Improvements installed within the Common Area from time to time by Declarant or the Association.
 Section 5.2. Delegation to Managing Agent. The Association hereby delegates the day-to-day performance of
the maintenance, repair, and replacement obligations set forth in Section 5.1 to its Managing Agent, being, as of
the date of this Declaration, Sagebrook Community Management LLC, a Nevada limited-liability company
having offices at 6280 S. Pecos Road, Suite 300, Las Vegas, NV 89120. The Managing Agent shall perform
such obligations pursuant to and in accordance with the written management agreement entered into between
the Association and the Managing Agent (the "Management Agreement"), which Management Agreement may
be renewed, replaced, or terminated by the Board in accordance with its terms and applicable law.

Section 5.3. Scope of Managing Agent Obligation. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the
Managing Agent is charged with and shall perform, in the name and on behalf of the Association:

(a) all routine and non-routine maintenance, repair, and replacement of the landscaping within all Common Area
parcels, including any turf, any planting, and any irrigation infrastructure, as and where installed by Declarant or
subsequently installed by or on behalf of the Association;

(b) the maintenance, repair, and replacement of all playground amenities located within any Common Area
parcel, as and where installed, including inspection for safety compliance and the replacement of resilient
surfacing and impact-attenuating materials;

(c) the procurement, supervision, and payment of qualified landscape maintenance contractors, irrigation
service contractors, playground safety inspectors, and other trades as required to discharge the foregoing
obligations;

(d) the maintenance of records of all such maintenance, repair, and replacement work; and

(e) periodic reporting to the Board with respect to the condition of the Common Area and any recommended
capital repair or replacement work.

Section 5.4. Assessments; Funding. The costs of performing the obligations set forth in this Article V shall be
borne by the Association and funded through regular and, if required, special assessments levied against the
Lots in accordance with this Declaration, the Bylaws, and NRS Chapter 116. The Managing Agent shall
administer the collection and application of such assessments in accordance with the Management Agreement.

Section 5.5. Owner Obligation with Respect to Lots. Each Owner shall be responsible for the maintenance,
repair, and replacement of all Improvements located upon such Owner's Lot, and the Association shall have no
obligation to maintain any portion of any Lot. Nothing in this Article V shall be construed to place upon the
Association or the Managing Agent any obligation with respect to any Improvement located within any Lot.

Section 5.6. Standard of Maintenance. All Common Area Improvements shall be maintained in a first-class,
safe, sanitary, and attractive condition consistent with the standard originally installed by Declarant, and
consistent with all applicable laws, ordinances, and codes of Clark County, the State of Nevada, and the United
States.

Section 5.7. Right of Entry. The Association, the Managing Agent, and their respective employees, agents,
and contractors shall have the right at all reasonable times to enter upon the Common Area (and, upon prior
notice except in an emergency, upon any Lot to the extent necessary to reach the Common Area or to abate a
nuisance affecting the Common Area) for the purposes of performing the maintenance, repair, and replacement
obligations set forth in this Article V.



                                  ARTICLE VI. GENERAL PROVISIONS
 Section 6.1. Covenants Running with the Land. The covenants, conditions, restrictions, easements,
assessments, charges, and liens set forth in this Declaration shall run with and bind the Property, and shall inure
to the benefit of and be enforceable by the Declarant, the Association, and each Owner, and their respective
legal representatives, heirs, successors, and assigns.

Section 6.2. Term. The term of this Declaration shall be perpetual, subject to termination or amendment as
expressly provided herein and by NRS Chapter 116.

Section 6.3. Amendment. Except as otherwise expressly reserved to Declarant herein, this Declaration may be
amended only by the affirmative vote or written consent of Owners representing not less than sixty-seven
percent (67%) of the total voting power of the Association, and shall be effective upon recordation of the
amendment in the Office of the Clark County Recorder.

Section 6.4. Enforcement. Enforcement of this Declaration shall be by any proceeding at law or in equity by the
Association, Declarant, or any Owner against any person or entity violating or attempting to violate any provision
hereof, either to restrain violation or to recover damages, or both. Failure by the Association, Declarant, or any
Owner to enforce any provision hereof shall in no event be deemed a waiver of the right to do so thereafter.

Section 6.5. Severability. Invalidation of any one of these covenants or restrictions by judgment or court order
shall not affect any other provisions, which shall remain in full force and effect.

Section 6.6. Governing Law. This Declaration shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws
of the State of Nevada, including without limitation NRS Chapter 116.

Section 6.7. Notices. Any notice required or permitted to be given to any Owner under this Declaration shall be
deemed to have been properly given when delivered personally or when deposited in the United States mail,
postage prepaid, addressed to the Owner at the mailing address for such Owner on file with the Association.

Section 6.8. Conflict. In the event of any conflict between this Declaration and the Articles or the Bylaws, this
Declaration shall control. In the event of any conflict between this Declaration and any applicable provision of
NRS Chapter 116 that cannot be varied by agreement, the statute shall control.

Section 6.9. Successors of Managing Agent. The identity of the Managing Agent may be changed from time
to time by the Board without the necessity of any amendment to this Declaration; provided that, at all times, the
maintenance, repair, and replacement obligations set forth in Article V shall be performed by the Association
directly or by a qualified Managing Agent engaged by the Association.

from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, Inches, RGBColor
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH, WD_BREAK
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT
from docx.enum.section import WD_SECTION
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement

OUT = "/filesystem/Correspondence/Client/DSR_Ph3_L-4_Memo_10312026.docx"

BODY_PT = 10.5
TABLE_PT = 9
ACCENT = RGBColor(0x1F, 0x3A, 0x5F)
GREY = RGBColor(0x59, 0x59, 0x59)

doc = Document()

# ---------- page setup ----------
sec = doc.sections[0]
sec.page_width = Inches(8.5)
sec.page_height = Inches(11)
sec.left_margin = sec.right_margin = Inches(1.0)
sec.top_margin = Inches(0.8)
sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.8)

# ---------- base styles ----------
st = doc.styles["Normal"]
st.font.name = "Calibri"
st.element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn("w:eastAsia"), "Calibri")
st.font.size = Pt(BODY_PT)
st.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(5)
st.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.08

for name in ("List Bullet", "List Number"):
    s = doc.styles[name]
    s.font.name = "Calibri"
    s.font.size = Pt(BODY_PT)
    s.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    s.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.08


# ---------- helpers ----------
def set_cell_shading(cell, hex_fill):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    shd.set(qn("w:val"), "clear")
    shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto")
    shd.set(qn("w:fill"), hex_fill)
    tcPr.append(shd)


def set_cell_margins(table, top=40, bottom=40, left=80, right=80):
    tblPr = table._tbl.tblPr
    mar = OxmlElement("w:tblCellMar")
    for k, v in (("top", top), ("bottom", bottom), ("left", left), ("right", right)):
        el = OxmlElement(f"w:{k}")
        el.set(qn("w:w"), str(v))
        el.set(qn("w:type"), "dxa")
        mar.append(el)
    tblPr.append(mar)


def remove_table_borders(table):
    tblPr = table._tbl.tblPr
    borders = OxmlElement("w:tblBorders")
    for edge in ("top", "left", "bottom", "right", "insideH", "insideV"):
        el = OxmlElement(f"w:{edge}")
        el.set(qn("w:val"), "nil")
        borders.append(el)
    tblPr.append(borders)


def keep_row_together(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    cant = OxmlElement("w:cantSplit")
    trPr.append(cant)


def repeat_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    th = OxmlElement("w:tblHeader")
    trPr.append(th)


def para_border_bottom(p, sz=8, color="1F3A5F", space=1):
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    pbdr = OxmlElement("w:pBdr")
    b = OxmlElement("w:bottom")
    b.set(qn("w:val"), "single")
    b.set(qn("w:sz"), str(sz))
    b.set(qn("w:space"), str(space))
    b.set(qn("w:color"), color)
    pbdr.append(b)
    pPr.append(pbdr)


def para_box(p, color="7F7F7F"):
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    pbdr = OxmlElement("w:pBdr")
    for edge in ("top", "left", "bottom", "right"):
        b = OxmlElement(f"w:{edge}")
        b.set(qn("w:val"), "single")
        b.set(qn("w:sz"), "6")
        b.set(qn("w:space"), "4")
        b.set(qn("w:color"), color)
        pbdr.append(b)
    pPr.append(pbdr)


def add_runs(p, parts, size=None, color=None):
    """parts: list of str or (str, dict) where dict may have bold/italic."""
    for part in parts:
        if isinstance(part, tuple):
            text, fmt = part
        else:
            text, fmt = part, {}
        r = p.add_run(text)
        r.bold = fmt.get("bold", False)
        r.italic = fmt.get("italic", False)
        if size:
            r.font.size = Pt(size)
        if fmt.get("size"):
            r.font.size = Pt(fmt["size"])
        if color is not None:
            r.font.color.rgb = color
        if fmt.get("color") is not None:
            r.font.color.rgb = fmt["color"]
    return p


def para(parts, style=None, space_after=None, align=None, keep_next=False, size=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style=style)
    if isinstance(parts, str):
        parts = [parts]
    add_runs(p, parts, size=size)
    if space_after is not None:
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(space_after)
    if align is not None:
        p.alignment = align
    if keep_next:
        p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
    return p


def heading(text):
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(9)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(3)
    p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
    r = p.add_run(text)
    r.bold = True
    r.font.size = Pt(11.5)
    r.font.color.rgb = ACCENT
    return p


def bullet(parts):
    return para(parts, style="List Bullet")


def numbered(parts):
    return para(parts, style="List Number")


def data_table(headers, rows, widths, align=None, bold_rows=(), shade_rows=(), font_pt=TABLE_PT):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    t.style = "Table Grid"
    t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    t.autofit = False
    set_cell_margins(t)
    hdr = t.rows[0]
    repeat_header(hdr)
    keep_row_together(hdr)
    for i, h in enumerate(headers):
        c = hdr.cells[i]
        c.text = ""
        p = c.paragraphs[0]
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
        p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
        r = p.add_run(h)
        r.bold = True
        r.font.size = Pt(font_pt)
        r.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
        set_cell_shading(c, "1F3A5F")
        c.vertical_alignment = WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
        if align and align[i] == "R":
            p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
        elif align and align[i] == "C":
            p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    for ri, row in enumerate(rows):
        cells = t.add_row()
        keep_row_together(cells)
        for i, val in enumerate(row):
            c = cells.cells[i]
            c.text = ""
            p = c.paragraphs[0]
            p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
            p.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 1.0
            r = p.add_run(str(val))
            r.font.size = Pt(font_pt)
            if ri in bold_rows:
                r.bold = True
            if ri in shade_rows:
                set_cell_shading(c, "E8EDF3")
            c.vertical_alignment = WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
            if align and align[i] == "R":
                p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.RIGHT
            elif align and align[i] == "C":
                p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    for row in t.rows:
        for i, w in enumerate(widths):
            row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    # spacer after table
    sp = doc.add_paragraph()
    sp.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    sp.paragraph_format.line_spacing = 0.8
    return t


def add_field(run, instr):
    f1 = OxmlElement("w:fldChar")
    f1.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), "begin")
    it = OxmlElement("w:instrText")
    it.set(qn("xml:space"), "preserve")
    it.text = instr
    f2 = OxmlElement("w:fldChar")
    f2.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), "separate")
    t = OxmlElement("w:t")
    t.text = "1"
    f3 = OxmlElement("w:fldChar")
    f3.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), "end")
    run._r.append(f1)
    run._r.append(it)
    run._r.append(f2)
    run._r.append(t)
    run._r.append(f3)

- L-4 is a code requirement, and our own sheets already commit to it. Title 30 sec. 30.64.030(k) requires one medium-canopy street tree per 20 linear feet of frontage. On the 4,160 lf of frontage on our Sheet L-2, that is 208 street trees. L-1 shows 58, so we need to add 150.

- We can handle it as the redline of L-1 and L-2 you asked for. It uses the three species already on the plan (Desert Willow, Desert Museum Palo Verde, Thornless Mesquite, all on the 2022-approved palette) at the 20-ft spacing our sections already show. No new species, no change to the streetscape sections. It is still a real change: 150 trees, 0.92 ac-ft/yr of water and $75,000 of bond.

- Annual irrigation demand goes from 3.28 to 4.20 acre-feet per year (+0.92). HZ-1 turf (2.32) and HZ-2 drip planting (0.51) are unchanged. HZ-3 trees goes from 0.45 to 1.37.

- The bond basis goes from $5,357,000 to $5,432,000 (+$75,000). That covers 150 more 24-inch box trees plus a drip emitter assembly for each. The Section 9 lump sums are unchanged.

- To keep this from adding process, we need Comprehensive Planning to confirm in writing that the change is not “significant” under TM Condition 14. We should have that before we resubmit (Section 5).

2. What L-4 requires

The County’s shade and canopy guidance (CP-PW-GM-2025-04, March 2025) names sec. 30.64.030(k) as the binding standard and classes our streetscape palette as medium canopy, so the 1-per-20-lf rate applies. Each frontage is computed separately, rounded up to a whole tree, and summed. The 4,160 lf in the comment is the total from our own L-2 Streetscape Frontage Summary:

 ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Frontage Length (lf) Required (1 per 20 lf) Shown 08/21/2026 To add
 --------------------------------- ------------- ------------------------ ------------------ --------
 Windmill Ln. — Phase 3 frontage 2,560 128 34 94

 Interior collector — both sides 1,180 59 16 43

 Rainbow Blvd. — entry frontage 420 21 8 13

 Total street trees 4,160 208 58 150
 ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The 6 entry-monument Pistache and 10 park Evergreen Elms are not street trees and do not count toward the 208. They stay in the demand and the estimate unchanged.

We can’t push back on this comment. L-1 General Note 7, the L-2 sections and the L-2 streetscape notes all call for trees at 20 ft on center, but the plant schedule and plan graphics never followed through (58 trees on 4,160 lf is about one every 72 ft). TM Condition 25 requires the street frontage tree standard in effect at submittal. Condition 28 requires the irrigation demand worksheet to be updated for any palette revision before landscape approval.

There are two routes to a lower count, and I don’t recommend either for this resubmittal. Large-canopy species at one per 30 lf (also sec. 30.64.030(k)) would need 140 trees (86 / 40 / 14). But that changes the streetscape species, which Planning would likely treat as a significant change, and staff would expect a shade coverage exhibit to support it. An Alternative Standards request under sec. 30.64.050 needs a discretionary written approval from Planning, which puts another review on the critical path.

3. Annual irrigation demand

This follows the method in Ocotillo’s Water Budget and Irrigation Demand Worksheet (08/15/2026). Rates are 5.5 ft/yr for spray turf, 1.0 ft/yr for drip planting and 2,000 gallons per tree per year. Each hydrozone is rounded to two decimals, and the total is the sum of the rounded hydrozones.

 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Hydrozone 08/21/2026 submittal ac-ft/yr With L-4 ac-ft/yr Change
 --------------------------------------- --------------------------------------- ---------- ---------------------------------------- ---------- --------
 HZ-1 Common-area park turf (Parcel A) 18,400 sf × 5.5 ft/yr 2.32 No change 2.32 0.00

 HZ-2 Common-area drip planting 22,200 sf × 1.0 ft/yr 0.51 No change 0.51 0.00

 HZ-3 Trees 74 trees × 2,000 gal = 148,000 gal/yr 0.45 224 trees × 2,000 gal = 448,000 gal/yr 1.37 +0.92

 Total annual irrigation demand 3.28 4.20 +0.92
 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

With L-4, HZ-3 is 208 street + 6 entry monument + 10 park trees = 224. The new trees go on point-source emitters in the existing drip strips, so the HZ-2 area does not change. HZ-1 and HZ-2 are held as drawn on 08/21 to isolate L-4, and both will move with the park decision (Section 6). Summing unrounded volumes would give 3.29 and 4.21. The workbooks total the rounded hydrozones, and Bea’s revised worksheet should do the same so the figures tie.

4. Bond basis

Prices come from the Clark County Uniform Unit Cost Schedule (effective 01/01/2026), as in our 10/10/2026 estimate:

 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Estimate line 10/10/2026 estimate With L-4 Change
 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --------------------- -------------------- -------------
 7.09 Tree, 24-inch box, street frontage + entry ($485.00 EA) 64 EA $31,040.00 214 EA $103,790.00 +$72,750.00

 7.42 Point-source drip emitter assembly ($12.50 EA; one per tree, L-1 Detail 4) 750 EA $9,375.00 900 EA $11,250.00 +$1,875.00

 Section 6 subtotal — Landscape and Irrigation $389,340.00 $463,965.00 +$74,625.00

 Construction subtotal, Sections 1–8 $4,856,565.75 $4,931,190.75 +$74,625.00

 Section 9 allowances (lump sums per Addendum No. 1) $500,000.00 $500,000.00 $0.00

 Total before rounding $5,356,565.75 $5,431,190.75 +$74,625.00

 Engineer’s estimate = bond basis (rounded up to next $1,000, Sched. 12.02) $5,357,000 $5,432,000 +$75,000
 ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Schedule Sec. 7 note (b) requires street-frontage trees at no less than the 24-inch box price. The Section 9 allowances are lump sums, so they do not grow with the added work. Under TM Condition 8, the performance bond is posted at this amount with the Phase 3 SIA before recordation. Any separately required labor-and-material bond is posted at the same amount. We will reissue the estimate as Revision 1, re-sealed by Jonathan Kessler, with the resubmittal (A-6). For the surety broker, I would use $5,432,000 as the working number. I’d also ask for capacity to about $6.1 million until the Section 9 item in Section 6 is confirmed.

5. Process and schedule

TM Condition 14 sends “any significant change to approved plans, including but not limited to landscape and streetscape treatments in common areas” to a design-review hearing before the Enterprise TAB and the Planning Commission. At the June pre-app, Odette Marchetti said Planning would decide significance on the actual change, using a red-line comparison against the 2022-approved palette. A-3 asks us to coordinate with Planning before we resubmit. The L-4 redline adds quantity only. It keeps the species and sections already on L-2, at the same 20-ft spacing used on the approved Phase 1 & 2 streetscape, so we expect Planning to find it not significant. It is Planning’s call, though. A written determination now is our cheapest protection against the question coming back at approval.

The calendar has no room if the answer goes the other way. The 11/18 TAB cutoff (10/28) has passed. The next TAB is 12/16 (application by 11/25), and the Planning Commission would follow it. None of that finishes before 12/18. By our reading of NRS 278.360 as quoted in the TM approval letter, the Phase 3 map must be presented within two years of the 12/23/2024 recording of the Phase 1 & 2 map, which makes the deadline 12/23/2026. Silver Butte’s 10/26 email gave 03/14/2028, but that date applies the first-map period plus an extension. Extensions are discretionary and can only be applied for after a period expires. We are confirming the date with Planning in writing (M-1). Please plan on 12/23/2026 until then.

The LVVWD will-serve (LVVWD-WS-2026-3341, 07/22/2026) covers “the 60 residential lots and associated common-area irrigation demand indicated in the developer’s submittal.” TM Condition 21 requires it to be current at recordation. We will send LVVWD the revised demand and confirm the letter stands. U-2 requires current letters with the resubmittal anyway.

6. What could still move these numbers

- Frontage lengths. The 4,160 lf is our approximate L-2 figure, measured along the landscape strips. The guidance measures along the property line abutting each street, and staff check that against the final map. Our tabulation leaves out 80 ft of the 2,640-ft Windmill boundary at the detention parcel. The C-2 control points also put the Rainbow Blvd. boundary at about 665 ft, against the 420 lf we counted. Counting both in full would make the requirement 225 trees (+17), which adds about $8,000 to the bond and 0.11 ac-ft/yr to HZ-3. Bea and our survey group will reconcile the frontage to FM-26-100290 and show it by frontage on L-1. It is better for us to set this number than to have staff reset it in round two.

- Park turf (L-2/L-3). HZ-1 (2.32 ac-ft/yr, more than half the revised total) and the estimate’s turf line (item 7.16, $39,560) are carried as drawn. The SNWA bulletin (WRC-2024-07, Sec. 2) makes the single-family carve-out lot-based and places HOA park parcels outside it. With the playground cut, L-3 describes the lawn as passive use, and Sec. 3.2 says passive use is not functional turf. Unit Cost Schedule Sec. 7 note (a) also keeps nonfunctional turf out of the bond estimate. I don’t think L-2 can be closed on the exemption. I’d like to go through the bulletin with you and Adrienne before the L-2 response is written. The park decision will move demand more than L-4 does, and we will re-run both numbers on the final park scheme.

- Section 9 allowances. Under Addendum No. 1, agreed lump sums replace the Sec. 11 percentages only where the Department agreed to them before bonding (11.05). Item 11.02 drops out only where executed agreements show that the owner is carrying design and inspection (11.06). If Public Works applies the default percentages at approval, the revised basis becomes $5,671,000 (5% + 10%, with 11.02 owner-carried) or $6,066,000 (all defaults). The Department’s concurrence and the executed agreements should go in the file with Revision 1.

- Shade coverage. The guidance also applies a 30% streetscape shade-coverage target at 15-year canopy. It is shown on a Shade Coverage Exhibit, which we did not submit. If 208 trees fall short, staff will expect more trees or larger-canopy species.

- Placement and root barriers. Trees can’t go in utility easements without the utility’s consent (L-1 Note 12) or in sight-visibility zones (TM Condition 6). The Phase 3 map grants a 10-ft P.U.E. across the front of every lot, and the joint-trench lateral runs in the P.U.E. along the collector. A blocked tree should be made up elsewhere on the same frontage or cleared with the utility. It should not go through an Alternative Standards request. L-1 Detail 6 also calls for a root barrier at each street tree next to a walk. Neither estimate carries it, and the Schedule has no unit price for it. If Public Works wants it bonded, we would document a price under Sched. 12.04.

7. Next steps

 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 # Action Owner Target
 --- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------- ------------------
 1 Approve the L-4 approach in Section 1; carry $5,432,000 as the working bond number with the broker Callaway (Nokes) 11/04

 2 Redline L-1/L-2: 208 street trees, schedule matched to the plotted count (L-6), by-frontage tabulation on L-1, red-line palette comparison for Planning; revised Water Budget and Irrigation Demand Worksheet (HZ-3 = 224 trees) Ocotillo (Cortland) 11/04

 3 Reconcile frontage to FM-26-100290; shade coverage exhibit; easement and sight-zone check of all 208 locations Ocotillo / Sundial survey 11/06

 4 Request Planning’s written Condition 14 determination on the L-4 revision; confirm the NRS 278.360 date (M-1) Sundial (Braddock) Request by 11/04

 5 Engineer’s Estimate Revision 1 at the revised basis; Section 9 concurrence and executed agreements to file Sundial (Braddock / Kessler); Callaway 11/06

 6 Park program decision (L-2/L-3); meeting with counsel on L-2 Callaway 11/07

 7 Send revised common-area demand to LVVWD; confirm the will-serve stands (U-2) Sundial (Braddock) 11/13
 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I’ll call you Monday to walk through this. The draft L-4 matrix response is attached.

_________________________________

Max Braddock

Project Manager, Sundial Engineering & Survey

mbraddock@sundialensv.com · (702) 555-0144

steps.message:
I've written the memo to Callaway, dated 10/31/2026 with a signature block for you. The headline numbers: L-4 adds 150 street trees, which raises annual irrigation demand from 3.28 to 4.20 ac-ft/yr and the bond basis from $5,357,000 to $5,432,000. It's about 4–5 pages, and the draft L-4 matrix response is attached as Attachment A.

**What L-4 requires:** The comment holds up. Title 30 sec. 30.64.030(k) requires one medium-canopy tree per 20 lf of frontage. On our own 4,160 lf that's 208 street trees (Windmill 128, collector 59, Rainbow 21), against 58 shown. Our sheets already call for trees at 20 ft on center; the plant schedule and plan graphics just don't show them.

The memo recommends adding the trees as a redline of L-1 and L-2, using the same three species. No new species and no change to the sections, which keeps it as close to Nokes's "clerical" request as possible.

**Annual irrigation demand, by hydro-zone (ac-ft/yr), rounded the way the workbooks do:**

| Hydro-zone | Now | With L-4 |
|---|---|---|
| HZ-1 Park turf | 2.32 | 2.32 |
| HZ-2 Drip planting | 0.51 | 0.51 |
| HZ-3 Trees (74 → 224 trees) | 0.45 | 1.37 |
| **Total** | **3.28** | **4.20 (+0.92)** |

Adding the unrounded values would give 4.21; the memo notes this so nobody "corrects" it later.

**Bond basis:**
- **Added items:** 150 more 24-inch box trees at $485 (+$72,750). I also added one $12.50 drip emitter per tree (+$1,875), because Detail 4 on L-1 calls for one per tree. Without the emitters the total would be $5,430,000.
- **Section 9:** the $500,000 lump sums don't change.
- **Total:** rounded up to the next $1,000, the bond basis is **$5,432,000 (+$75,000)**.

**Check these before you sign — the memo takes positions on all of them:**
1. **Turf exemption (L-2):** The memo tells Nokes that L-2 can't be closed on Adrienne's single-family exemption. That's because the SNWA bulletin makes the exemption lot-based and puts HOA park parcels outside it. This goes against his instruction to use her memo and move on.
2. **Map deadline:** The memo puts the deadline at **12/23/2026**, two years after the Phase 1 & 2 map recorded. This contradicts Silver Butte's 03/2028 date. It's flagged as subject to Planning's written confirmation (M-1).
3. **Planning sign-off:** The memo asks Planning to confirm in writing that the tree redline is not a "significant change" under TM Condition 14. If Planning disagrees, the earliest TAB is 12/16, which can't finish before 12/18.
4. **Section 9 lump sums:** I found no record that Public Works agreed to the lump sums, which Addendum No. 1 requires. If the default percentages apply instead, the basis would be $5.67M–$6.07M. On that basis the memo suggests asking the surety broker for capacity to about $6.1M.
5. **Frontage length:** 4,160 lf is our approximate landscape-strip figure. Measured along the property line, the Windmill boundary is 2,640 ft and the Rainbow boundary is about 665 ft (from the C-2 control points). Counting both in full would mean up to 225 trees: about +$8,000 on the bond and +0.11 ac-ft/yr.

The memo also adds a "call you Monday" line, since Nokes asked for calls rather than email. The cc list is Lee Chastain, Kessler, Priya Sarwal, Bea Cortland and the project file; Adrienne isn't on it.

The file is at `Correspondence/Client/DSR_Ph3_L-4_Memo_10312026.docx`.
